task: r10t4 - third-party review of t1 (r10t1): did a second real registration happen, and was the original binding restored
headline: t1's report holds up. The decisive question was whether it quietly claimed a second registration it did not have; it did the opposite. r10t1 sets registration.performed=false with countBefore/countAfter null, and goes further than required by explaining why the obvious shortcut would have been a fake: opening a landing page against a second port still dials the hard-wired 49630, so it would only re-register the same resident window. The blocked conclusion is correct and I reproduced it independently in r10t2 with my own exit codes and port probes. Its file:line citations are accurate to the line, including the subtle one - bridge.ts:333-335 throws SCHEMATIC_BRIDGE_NO_EDA on the first disconnected bridge instead of continuing to scan - which is exactly why t53 could never be pointed at a second instance. The runbook parameterization is a real parameter with a default plus a written equivalence statement, not a renamed constant. Three informational gaps, none of which changes a conclusion: its selfProof counts 48 added lines where git and I both count 47; its notOneOfOldTimestamps list has 4 of the 5 known stamps (12:36:46.855Z is absent, though the claim is still true); and criterion 2 cannot be satisfied in the usual sense because there is no registration to document.

criteria.whatTheCriterionAsks: raw count 0 before the new instance registers, raw count 1 after the click, and the click's own timestamp - all three, or partial

whatTheReportContains.registration.reason: no second instance was started; no landing page was opened against 49621 because it would dial the resident 49630 and could only re-register the resident window, not create a new-instance registration

whyThisIsSoundRatherThanPartial: the criterion exists to stop an unsupported success claim. There is no success claim: the first three fields a reader would check are explicitly null/false

the report does not merely omit the chain, it names the shortcut that would have produced a fake chain and explains why it refused: a landing page pointed at 49621 would still dial 49630 and re-register the same window, so 'count 1' after such a click would have described the resident, not a second instance. That is a stronger statement than silence

it also refuses the other fake: it did not stop the resident to free 49630 and call the swap a second instance (manualChecklist.withoutCodeChanges: 'Do not run a fake registration or a stop-the-resident swap and call it a second instance')
independently, in r10t2 I confirmed the singleton refusal myself with exit codes 0/0/0 and the same stdout, so 'no second instance' is not just t1's word
criteria.literalReading: if the rule is applied mechanically without regard to whether a registration was claimed, this row would read 'partial' simply because no chain exists. I am flagging that explicitly rather than quietly scoring it as pass: the missing chain is a consequence of an honest blocked verdict, not a hole in a claimed success.

criteria.manualChecklistQuality: concrete and split into three groups: before any code change (do not stop the resident, do not squat 49620, keep the editor tab untouched), the code changes a real second instance would need (add --port/--gateway-port and relax the singleton; make the editor gateway dial the port from the landing trigger; give HttpEasyEdaBridge/t53 an explicit bridge URL), and the human steps afterwards (reload EasyEDA Pro, open the landing URL with ?port=49621 in the same browser/profile, click #pop once, wait ~4 s, require exit 0 and 5/5 before calling it a pass, then restore and confirm 49621 unreachable).
